subject: Custom log window proposal and next steps for Orbis Health

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — data handling and retention needs

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we’re aligned and to capture agreed next steps: 

Summary of ask from Orbis Health: 
- Primary concern: PII in request payloads (patient identifiers) and minimizing storage surface for regulated workloads.
- Regulatory constraint: need auditable evidence of feature usage for 180 days for certain investigations, but prefer minimal raw request storage.
- Preferred deployment options under consideration: Hosted with strict retention controls, or Redwood Private (VPC) for stronger isolation.

What Redwood can do (high level):
- Offer configurable retention windows per data class (e.g., request bodies, request metadata, system logs).
- Provide PII redaction/field-level hashing for fields you identify as sensitive.
- Provide an audit trail (hashed event records) that can be retained longer while request bodies are truncated/evicted sooner.

Immediate next steps we agreed on: 
1) Elena: send the list of fields you consider PII and any internal retention policy constraints (format: CSV).
2) Redwood (me + Marissa): share a short matrix outlining feasible retention configurations and business/technical tradeoffs.
3) Marissa/Dylan: estimate delta in cost and lead time between hosted retention policies vs Redwood Private.

Attachments: redwood-retention-options.pdf (options + tradeoffs) and prod-logging-matrix.pdf (example logging categories).

I’ll circulate a tailored proposal once we have the PII field list. Goal: give you a concrete configuration you can run past security and procurement early next week.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0122

2) Audit evidence: for compliance we must be able to prove an action occurred (audit event) up to 180 days. Does your hashed-audit approach meet that requirement? Do you store the salt/keys on Redwood side or can we keep the keys in our KMS?

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — data handling and retention needs

Karthik / Dylan —

Drafted three practical options to present to Orbis (short bullets, we can expand for SOW):

Option A — Minimum-hosted (fastest / lowest ops):
- Hosted API; request bodies retained 7 days; metadata and request headers retained 90 days; PII fields redacted at ingest.
- Audit events (hashed IDs) exported daily to customer-managed S3 for 180 days.
- Tradeoff: some live debugability lost after 7 days.

Option B — Hosted + hardened controls (middle ground):
- Hosted with in-memory ephemeral handling for request bodies; raw bodies not written to disk (0-disk-retention) but transient in memory for inference.
- Structured audit events (no raw PII) retained 180 days in encrypted logs.
- Requires additional validation on our side around memory sweeping and cache windows.

Option C — Private deployment (highest isolation):
- Full Private (VPC) deployment, customer KMS for salt/keys, customizable retention per log class (you can specify 7/30/180 days).
- Longer lead time and higher cost but meets strict data residency & KMS control requirements.

Recommendation: present Options A and B as the pragmatic starting points while we scope C if procurement/legal asks for KMS ownership.

I’ll draft cost delta estimates by Monday and a short SOW paragraph for each option.

-Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 11:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal — tailored retention windows & recommended path

Elena / Tom —

Following Marissa’s notes, we put together two pragmatic configurations for Orbis with pros/cons. Below are the technical commitments and preliminary cost implications. 

Proposal 1 (Practical, Hosted-first):
- Request bodies: 0-disk retention (transient in-memory only) for 24 hours, then truncated.
- Request metadata (timestamps, non-PII headers): 90 days retention.
- Audit trail: HMAC-hashed event records kept 180 days in Redwood encrypted logs; salt stored by Redwood but you can request rotation schedule.
- Cost: ~+12% on hosted baseline due to ephemeral handling and extra encryption; no infra changeouts.

Proposal 2 (Balanced, Hosted w/ longer audit + customer KMS):
- Request bodies: not persisted to disk (ephemeral memory).
- Short-lived encrypted snapshots (7 days) of request metadata for troubleshooting.
- Audit trail: 180-day hashed events; keys managed in your KMS (we integrate with Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS) — this requires Private control plane or RBAC change for key escrow.
- Cost: ~+22% vs baseline; partial private controls, faster than full Private deployment.

Technical notes / constraints:
- \"0-retention\" on disk does not remove in-memory KV caches while inference is happening; we guarantee sweep/eviction windows and can provide attestations for sweep behavior.
- For forensic needs where you need raw bodies, we can provide an opt-in export workflow with strict access logging and limited TTL.

Attached: custom-retention-SOW-draft.docx (a short SOW paragraph for each option). Also linking our SOC2 report: https://redwood.app/soc2-report-link

Could you confirm which path you prefer (Proposal 1 / Proposal 2 / explore Private)? Once you confirm, we’ll:
- Lock technical acceptance criteria for security to include in SOW.
- Produce a pricing amendment and timeline for legal/procurement review.

Thanks —
Karthik
